html:
The Crnojević printing house was a press set up at Cetinje by Đurađ Crnojević, ruler of Zeta, in 1493. In 1494 it printed the Oktoih, the first book printed in Cyrillic among the South Slavs.

The press was run by the monk Makarije, who probably learned the craft in Venice, and it printed liturgical books for the Orthodox church. It worked only a few years: Zeta fell to the Ottomans in 1496 and Đurađ fled to Venice. Makarije later printed books in Wallachia. The press came only some forty years after Gutenberg, and it made Montenegro an early centre of Slavic printing. Copies of the Oktoih survive in libraries across Europe.
